body.statement: Suppose \(m\) is odd and no allowed edge \(j\to i\) has \(A_{ii}=A_{jj}=0\). Then every nonempty \(\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\) is a singleton. Its diagonal is \(A_{ii}=B_{ii}^{1/m}\); its allowed off-diagonal entries are recovered in increasing endpoint gap by \(A_{ij}=\{B_{ij}-R_{ij,m}(A)\}/C_m(A_{ii},A_{jj})\); and its diagonal innovations are recovered in increasing \(i\) by \(D_{ii}=\{Q_{ii}-\sum_{j<i}D_{jj}\sum_{r=0}^{m-1}(A^r)_{ij}^2\}/\sum_{r=0}^{m-1}A_{ii}^{2r}\). Full substitution into forbidden entries and off-diagonal covariance equations is necessary and sufficient for compatibility. Consequently \(\mathcal H_{uv}(B,Q;G)=\{h_{uv}\}\).
body.justification: This is the constructive point-identification half of the parity frontier.
body.gap: Gong et al. require non-Gaussian shocks for recovery; Smith computes a chosen root but does not prove uniqueness after graph and innovation-covariance checks.
body.consumer: Fine-grid policy or scientific impulse analysis can use a closed-form transfer even though only every \(m\)-th state was recorded.
